title: CI runs the Go and Python suites with machine-readable output at the checked-out commit, and assure record reads an outcome for every automated test record
The provider's attestation action signs the proof run with the commit as subject and keeps it
An outcome names an ID the spec does not have, so assure record exits non-zero and writes nothing
On a pull request, CI runs assure judge change, which measures the coverage at the change's commit and at the base head
assure judge change fetches the proof run attestation for the change's commit from the provider and verifies it
A share fell or a proof did not pass, so the verdict names each cause and the check fails
The release workflow runs assure judge release at the commit to release, which measures the coverage and verifies the proof run there
The provider's attestation action signs the passed verdict with the commit as subject and keeps it
A share is below 100% or a proof did not pass, so the workflow stops and publishes no release
The platform engineer runs assure ledger for a commit, and STEGO fetches and verifies the proof runs from the provider and prints each test record with its result and where it last passed
An attestation fails verification, so the ledger shows no result for it and says why
The service author runs stego deps, and STEGO resolves the modules and writes go.mod and go.sum
Generated code is out of date, so stego deps refuses and names apply
Resolution stops part way, and stego recover completes or rolls back the module files
The operator runs build download for a revision, and STEGO writes the zips and the cache record
A zip whose hash differs from go.sum stops the download, and STEGO names the module, its version, the hash go.sum states and the hash it found
A module the proxy cannot supply stops the download, and STEGO names the module and its version
A target folder that exists or an SDK that is not the archetype's stops the download before any network call, and STEGO names the folder or the SDK digest it expected and found
The download is interrupted, so STEGO removes its work folder and leaves no cache and no record, and the operator runs it again
The operator runs stego build for a revision with its module cache, and STEGO builds twice, offline, compares, and writes the record and both SBOMs
A missing module, a different SDK or two different builds stop the build, and STEGO names why
The operator runs build verify on an executable, and STEGO reports whether it matches the trusted record
The operator runs build verify-source on a source snapshot, and STEGO reports whether it matches
The record's canonical bytes do not hash to the trusted digest, so STEGO refuses the record before it reads the artifact, and names the digest it expected and the digest it found
The executable differs from the record, so STEGO names each digest and each build setting that differs, with the recorded and the found value, and exits non-zero
The source snapshot differs from the record's inventory, so STEGO names each path that is missing, added or changed, and exits non-zero
The record or the artifact cannot be read, so STEGO reports a failed check, not a pass, and names the file
The operator runs image build from the trusted build, and STEGO writes a scratch image and its record
The provider's trusted signer signs the image and attaches both SBOMs
An untrusted build record or CA bundle stops image build
The operator runs image publish, and STEGO pushes the image and reads it back
A consumer runs image retrieve, and STEGO checks the image, its build and its signature
The local image does not match its record, so STEGO refuses to push and names what differs
The repository carries a tag, the CA bundle digest differs or the credentials are missing, so STEGO refuses before it opens a connection and names the input
The push fails or the read-back differs, so STEGO names the digest it pushed and the digest it read, writes no publication record, and the operator runs publish again
The retrieved image differs from its record, its build record is not trusted or its signature is not by the trusted signer, so STEGO writes the image nowhere and names the check that failed
The consumer names a repository by tag or a CA bundle whose digest is not trusted, so STEGO refuses to retrieve before it opens a connection and names the input
The author names the archetype for the new service
STEGO writes the declaration with the archetype's smallest example content, and a folder for fills
An archetype the registry does not hold is refused, with the archetypes it does hold
A declaration already present stops the scaffold, and no file changes
Asked for an empty scaffold, STEGO leaves the example content out and names every setting the author must supply

STEGO resolves the registry with generation's resolver under the apply lock, keeps the configuration bytes as written, and writes a configuration that names ./registry or the environment override as a local source when none exists
A symbolic link at a path the scaffold would write is refused, naming the path, and no file changes
The agent names the archetype it writes for
STEGO reports the active component set's components, each setting with its type and allowed values, and each slot, as structured data
The archetype is one the registry does not hold, so STEGO refuses to report and names the archetypes it does hold
The registry cannot be resolved as generation resolves it, so STEGO reports nothing and names the source and the pin it could not read
The author asks STEGO to check the declaration, and STEGO reports every fault or that there is none
A declaration that holds an acceptance past its date is refused, naming the component and the date
The agent reads each fault: the rule it breaks, its path, what was found and what is allowed
The agent changes the declaration at the path each fault names
The agent asks STEGO to check the declaration again
The check refuses the declaration again, so the agent compares the new faults with the old ones and repairs the faults that remain
The changed declaration no longer reads as one YAML document, so STEGO reports one fault with the line and column where reading stopped, and the agent repairs that place first
The platform engineer names the component digest and the checkouts to search
STEGO reads the committed record in each checkout, and names each service that pins the digest, with its version and digest
A checkout with generated output and no readable record is reported as unknown
The platform engineer runs stego fleet vex, and STEGO emits one OpenVEX statement per service and advisory, with the status affected, fixed or not_affected
The platform engineer changes one component, and the registry publishes its new digest
The platform engineer records the new digest as the successor of the old one, with the fail date and whether taking it needs a declaration or fill change
A consumer moves that component's pin alone and runs apply in Generating, and keeps its compiler pin
A supersession with no successor, no fail date or no statement of the change it needs is refused
The platform engineer releases a new runtime library version, moves the archetype's pin to it, and records the old version as superseded; each consumer takes it with a registry pin bump and a new run
The service author runs validate or plan
STEGO reports each superseded pin with its successor and fail date, and does not fail for that reason
Past its fail date, validate fails for the pin
Past its fail date, apply in Generating refuses to write unless the author overrides the pin by name
When STEGO cannot read the lifecycle records, it reports that it could not check, and does not report the pins as current
The platform engineer asks STEGO for every recorded service that pins the digest
The platform engineer records the withdrawal, with the future date after which the digest fails
After the date, validate fails for every service that still pins the digest
A withdrawal whose date is already past is refused
Apply in Generating refuses a new pin to a withdrawn digest at once, whatever the date of the withdrawal
The platform engineer names the commit to qualify
STEGO finds the checks run and the signed artifact run at exactly that commit, and requires a success conclusion for every required job
STEGO installs the published release through the consumer path, and cross-checks each asset digest against the qualified artifacts
A run from another commit, or a required job with no success conclusion, fails qualification
A release tag that points at another commit fails verification
STEGO fetches the release verdict attested at exactly that commit and verifies it passed
No passed release verdict is attested at that commit, so qualification fails
The operator names the release by its full source commit
The installer checks each asset digest and both signatures, and the signed record's platform, then puts the binary and its build record in place
The operator asks the installed compiler for its build identity, and it reports the identity it writes into a service's record
On any platform other than Linux amd64, the installer refuses before it downloads anything
The platform engineer names the checkouts, and STEGO computes each outcome measure from their committed records, with no network
STEGO prints each measure with the services behind it
A checkout without a readable record is named as unknown and counted against every share, not skipped
The service author runs stego apply, and STEGO writes platform-requirements.yaml with the rest of the generated files
A component states a need with an environment value in it, so apply refuses, names the component and the need, and writes nothing
Two components state one need with different shapes, so apply refuses, names both components and the need, and writes nothing
platform-requirements.yaml was edited by hand, so apply refuses it as a hand-edited generated file and names it, and the author moves the change into service.yaml
The operator runs stego env check on an environment file, by hand or in the platform repo's CI, and STEGO reports that it meets every requirement
A requirement is unmet or a value is mistyped, so STEGO names each one and exits non-zero
The environment file or platform-requirements.yaml cannot be read, so STEGO reports a failed check, not a pass, and names the file and the place
The environment file holds a value that no platform requirement names, so STEGO lists it as unused and reports that the environment meets every requirement
The service author runs stego apply, and STEGO writes the CI file for the provider the delivery stanza names
On a push, GitHub Actions runs the pinned reusable workflow, which runs the STEGO checks, stego build, stego image build and signs keyless
On a push, Konflux runs its standard pipeline from the offline Containerfile, then stego delivery check, and Tekton Chains signs
A STEGO check fails, so the pipeline stops and releases no image
The platform engineer releases a ci-pipeline version with the new pin, and each service author runs stego apply, which changes only the pin
The new reference is not pinned, so stego apply refuses it and names it
service.yaml sets a pipeline reference or a signer, so apply refuses it as an undeclared field and names the path
The CI file was edited by hand, so apply refuses the patch and names the file, and the author removes the edit or states that the run may replace it
The service author runs stego apply, and STEGO writes the Kubernetes base and the delivery object
STEGO writes the Argo CD Application from the delivery stanza
The operator checks the environment file and commits the overlay, and Argo CD applies base and overlay
The delivery stanza names a destination, a namespace or an overlay, so apply refuses it as an undeclared field, names the path, and writes nothing
service.yaml has no delivery stanza, so apply writes no Argo CD Application and says so in the plan, and the author adds the stanza when the service is to be delivered
stego env check finds an unmet requirement, so the GitOps flow stops before Argo CD syncs the overlay, and the operator completes the environment file and checks again
The agent runs fill create for the slot and collection, and STEGO writes a fill and a test that compile against the slot's contract
The agent writes the rule and its tests, binds the fill in the declaration, and runs stego test, and STEGO records the fill's evidence
A fill with no test file or a forbidden import gets no evidence, and STEGO names why
Plan finds a bound fill that implements another slot or serves another collection, and stops
The service author runs stego test, and STEGO records the evidence of each fill whose tests pass
The service author runs fill sign, and STEGO signs the evidence with the author's key and writes the sign-off
A fill's tests fail, so STEGO records no evidence and fill sign refuses it
A signature by a key that the SIGNERS file does not list leaves the fill unsigned, and plan stops
The agent runs registry fills for the slot, and STEGO lists each fill with its collection and standing
The slot is one no component of the active set declares, so STEGO refuses and names the slots the set does declare
No fill implements the slot, so STEGO says so by name and names fill create as the way to add one
A fill folder holds a fill.yaml STEGO cannot read, so the list shows it as unreadable with its fault, and the author repairs it
The service author runs fill status, and STEGO names each stale fill and what changed
The service author runs stego test, and STEGO records new evidence
The service author runs fill sign, and STEGO signs the new evidence
Plan or apply meets a stale fill, stops, and names it
The service author runs apply, and STEGO writes the generated files and the record together
The service author commits the record with the generated code
An interrupted apply leaves a journal, and plan, apply and drift refuse until the author runs recover
The platform engineer asks STEGO to check the record, and STEGO names every generated file that no longer matches its hash
A record that disagrees with itself, or that names a registry or compiler its state does not hold, is reported as broken
The service author moves the component's pin to the successor digest
The service author runs plan, and STEGO saves the plan and lists each file that the new digest changes
The service author runs apply, and STEGO changes only the files that the new digest affects
The service author reads the diff of the fix and commits it with the record
Apply names every generated file that no longer matches its hash, and writes nothing
When the author states on the command that the run may replace hand-edited files, apply replaces them
STEGO reports the standing of each pin, the successor included, and refuses to go on while any pin is withdrawn or past its fail date
Apply refuses a pin that is withdrawn or past its fail date, naming it and its successor, and the author moves it to a digest that stands
STEGO reports the qualification of each bound fill against the new contracts, and the author goes on only when every one is qualified
A fix that changes a slot contract leaves its fills stale, so the author requalifies them before apply
The author overrides the pin by name on the command with a reason, apply goes on, and the record names the override
The service author changes the declaration
STEGO reports the standing of each pin before the change is applied, and apply refuses a pin that is withdrawn or past its fail date unless the author overrides it by name
The service author runs apply, and STEGO plans in the same run and writes the changed files, deletes the files it no longer generates, and writes the record
The service author reads the diff of the declaration change and commits it with the declaration and the record
A failed validation, generator or assembly stops the run, STEGO names the failure, and no file changes
STEGO reports the qualification of each bound fill, and the author goes on only when every one is qualified and fits its binding
A bound fill that is not qualified or does not fit stops the run before apply, and the author requalifies or rebinds it
The service author runs plan, and STEGO saves the plan and lists each change
The service author reads the saved plan
The service author runs apply with the saved plan, and STEGO writes exactly what it names
An input, the record or a generated file changed after planning, so apply refuses the plan and the author plans again
Plan, apply and drift refuse while a journal is pending, and name recover
The service author runs recover, and STEGO completes the journal
A journaled file matches neither of its states, so recover names it and changes nothing
The service author runs stego assets on the build folder, and STEGO writes the checked bundle
An entry fails its checks, so STEGO names it and leaves the output as it was
The service author runs stego apply, and STEGO derives the architecture model and writes the view with the code
The service owner opens the view in a browser, selects elements and follows request flows
A component states no architecture role, so apply refuses to derive the view, names the component and the missing statement, and writes nothing
The service has no element for an aspect, so the view says that the aspect has no element yet, instead of an empty diagram
The service author runs stego apply after a change, and the diff of the architecture model shows how the service changed
The view or model was edited or is stale, so stego drift names it
The change leaves every element as it was, so the model file is byte-identical and the empty diff tells the reviewer that the shape did not change
The record cannot be read, so drift fails and names the record instead of reporting the view as current, and the author runs recover or restores the record
The author runs validate, and STEGO refuses the declaration version and names the versions the registry accepts
The author runs stego fix, and STEGO rewrites the declaration to the next accepted version and changes no other file
The author reviews the diff of the declaration, the only file the fixer changed, and runs plan, which lists each generated file the new version changes
The author runs apply, and STEGO writes the files and a record that states the new declaration version, from which the sweep names each service still on the old one
The fixer cannot rewrite a construct, so it names each one with its path and writes nothing, and the agent rewrites them by hand
The agent runs validate again, and STEGO accepts the declaration version or names the faults that remain
The declaration version is superseded past its fail date, so plan refuses the service, writes nothing, and names the version, its successor and the date
Apply refuses the same service for the same reason and writes nothing, until the author moves it with stego fix
The platform engineer defines each port the component provides that the registry does not hold yet
The platform engineer declares each slot the component offers, with its protobuf contract
The platform engineer adds the component with its config schema, its ports, its slots and its namespace, and STEGO accepts it before its generator runs
The platform engineer states each thing the emitted code must always do as an output contract, with the generator that builds it and the test that proves it
The platform engineer changes what the generator emits, and releases the component at a new version
A namespace that another component of the registry claims is refused, naming both components
A component that states no architecture role is refused, naming the component
A file the component emits is the same for every declaration, so the registry refuses the component as static and names the file
The platform engineer pins the common registry at one reference
The platform engineer names a local registry that adds the team's own parts, at one reference
STEGO composes the sources into one active set, and records the reference of each
A local part that would replace a common part is refused, naming the part and both registries

A composition with more than eight sources, two sources that supply one artifact name or input path, a symbolic link, or inputs over 64 MiB or 4,096 files is refused after every source is captured and before any is validated
A Git source without a full lower-case commit SHA, or a vendored checkout that is not at that commit, lacks Git metadata or holds modified, ignored or untracked files, is refused without a fetch

A namespace entry outside the active set, an empty or compiler-owned path, or a nonempty per-component pin is refused before any source is resolved, and an environment override of the sources is warned of
The platform engineer chooses the components the archetype includes, and the component that answers each port by default
STEGO accepts the archetype with its smallest example content, which a fresh declaration of it passes checking with
A required port with no provider, or with more than one, is refused, naming the port and every component involved
A component that is not ga is refused, naming the component and its stage
A mixin that brings a component that is not ga is refused, naming the component and its stage
The platform engineer gives the component a port name of its own, which no ga component provides
The platform engineer adds the component at stage alpha with the date it stops working, the outcome it serves, its references or why none exists, and its promise list as output contracts
A service that wants the component accepts it by name in its declaration, with a date of its own
A sunset date that is already past is refused
A component that states no outcome, no reference and no reasoning, or no contract, is refused with what is missing
The platform engineer reads every recorded service that uses the component
The platform engineer moves the component up to ga, which removes its sunset date and lets it take over the real port name
The platform engineer withdraws a component that will not graduate
STEGO reports every service that still uses a component past its sunset, and checking fails for each of them
The platform engineer records the security review, the benchmark and the design review at the component's digest, and the reference comparison at its contract set's digest
A component that lacks a piece of the quality bar, or whose reference comparison is stale or leaves a promise undecided, stays below ga, and STEGO names what is missing
A component that provides a port whose conformance tests it has not passed at its digest stays below ga, and STEGO names the port and the suite
The platform engineer records the benchmark as figures per reference, and STEGO compares them with the previous version's figures and names each figure that regressed
A benchmark recorded as free text, with no figure per reference, is refused, naming what each figure must hold
The service author runs registry promote, and STEGO copies the component at its digest into a checkout of the common registry at stage alpha
The service author opens the change to the common registry, and a platform engineer reviews and accepts it
The service author moves the service's pin to the promoted component, and regeneration changes no file
The common registry already holds a component of that name, so STEGO refuses and names it
The platform engineer names the port, what a provider undertakes to supply and the meaning of every field
The platform engineer names the port's conformance test suite, which every provider runs, and STEGO records the port
A provider passes the suite at its digest, and the pass is recorded as port conformance evidence, so the provider may graduate
A port name that is already defined is refused, naming the port, so a changed meaning takes a new name
A field with no meaning is refused, naming the field
The first provider of a port whose conformance suite is missing stays below ga, and STEGO names the port
A provider that has not passed the suite at its current digest stays below ga, and STEGO names the port and the suite
The platform engineer declares the slot on the component, with the protobuf service file that is its contract
The platform engineer changes the contract within Buf's FILE rules, and releases the component at a new version
A contract file that is missing or holds no service is refused, naming the slot and the file
A contract change that fails a FILE rule is refused when the slot is declared, naming the slot and each rule, unless the slot takes a new name
A release whose slot contract fails a FILE rule under the old slot name is refused, naming the slot and each rule, so old fills keep compiling
A slot that no generator of the component invokes is refused, naming the slot and the component
The platform engineer lists every component that provides or requires the port, with its stage
The platform engineer sets the ga provider the archetype answers the port with by default
No provider of the port is ga, so the choice is refused, naming the port and each provider with its stage
A provider that has not passed the port's conformance tests is below ga, so it cannot be the default, and STEGO names the suite it has not passed
